1	# LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon
     2	
     3	LeanAG Horizon is a multi-project Lean 4 and Mathlib workspace for formalizing algebraic
     4	geometry with [Archon Horizon](https://github.com/frenzymath/Archon-Horizon). Its central goal is
     5	the algebraic-geometry version of the [Algebraic Jacobian challenge](https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/583336-Autoformalization/topic/Jacobian.20challenge/near/587802685),
     6	proposed by Christian Merten after Kevin Buzzard's differential-geometry challenge.
     7	
     8	> [!IMPORTANT]
     9	> The workspace develops **two live routes** to the Algebraic Jacobian challenge. Follow the
    10	> project named by the active task rather than treating either route as reference-only.
    11	>
    12	> - `MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge` continues the ambitious Picard-scheme route, building
    13	>   representability by the Milne–Kollár construction of `Pic^r`, then `Pic^0` and the Albanese
    14	>   property. Its Grassmannian, graded-algebra and flattening-stratification substrate is sorry-free
    15	>   and still consumed, but the Quot-scheme endgame it was first written for is not the path being
    16	>   built. Since 2026-07-28 its headline is stated over an arbitrary base field, with
    17	>   representability asked of the étale-sheafified Picard functor and no rational-point hypothesis.
    18	> - `MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild` develops a cleaner curve-specialized route
    19	>   from protected target statements.
    20	
    21	The two projects share mathematical sources and supporting subprojects while keeping independent
    22	Lean roots, blueprints, and roadmaps. The rebuild is listed first in the workspace manifest as the
    23	default project; explicitly scoped tasks may and do advance the ambitious original route.

   101	- **Blueprint graphs (`hgraph`)** track declaration dependencies, proof status, comments, and the
   102	  ranked frontier for each project.
   103	- **Roadmap, tasks, and inbox** record strategy, scoped work, cross-session handoffs, and durable
   104	  failure memory.
   105	- **The workspace ledger** records coherent commits and powers the public dashboard's progress
   106	  and session views.
   107

   109	import, build the staged root from the ledger's current `HEAD` and insert only
   110	that line; do not stage the whole on-disk root, which may contain another
   111	session's uncommitted imports.
   112	
   113	The mathematical blueprint is kept separate from implementation journals. Lean-specific progress
   114	and failed approaches belong in graph comments, tasks, or the inbox, while the blueprint remains a
   115	timeless account of the mathematics.

   130	- **Supporting work:** a focused subproject under `SubProjects/` is appropriate when a reusable

`alternatingCofaceComplexIsoOfDelta` applied to `twistedComponent` and `twistedComponent_δ_square`

    (F : X.Modules) (hF : F.IsQuasicoherent)

    (AlgebraicTopology.alternatingCofaceMapComplex X'.Modules).obj

            (CechNerve (bcCover f g f' g' h 𝒰) ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g').obj F))) :=

three rounds as walled, with a correct diagnosis and a wrong conclusion:

- *diagnosis*, true: "nothing in the tree relates the Beck–Chevalley mate across a **change of

- *pricing*, also true: the alternative route needs "`pushPullMap` is the degenerate-square mate",

- *conclusion*, false: therefore the leaf is blocked on new mate infrastructure.

**The move.** A mate need not be *related* across squares if it can be *removed*. `mateEquiv` is
defined so that mathlib's `CategoryTheory.mateEquiv_counit` evaluates

    L₂.map ((mateEquiv adj₁ adj₂ α).app d) ≫ adj₂.counit.app _ = α.app _ ≫ H.map (adj₁.counit.app d)

— it computes `L.map (mate) ≫ counit` and **hands back the 2-cell `α` the mate was built from**. So
put the goal under the left adjoint and past the counit and the mate is gone, replaced by
pseudofunctor coherence (`pullbackComp`, `pullbackCongr`) plus single-adjunction counits, which trees
like this one do have. Cost here: one `rw` (`bareBC_pullback_counit`). No open immersion, no flatness,
not even cartesianness — cf. [[statement-decoration-vs-proof]].

**Getting the goal into that position is itself a lemma chain, not free.** Both sides landed in
`p_* p^*(−)`, the image of a right adjoint, so `homEquiv.symm.injective` reflects equality down from
`p^*` — and the *counit-composed* version of that cancellation is the one to use, because it is what
the mate law's left side looks like. Prove the weakest form; check the converse so you know it is a
change of vocabulary and not a weakening ([[reduction-needs-its-converse`]]).

**Two honest limits, both measured.** The elimination fired on only one side of my square (mate and
counit at the same index there; at the other index they are separated by a restriction map). And the
remaining step is **not** `Adjunction.counit_naturality`: that moves past the counit only maps already
of the form `R.map ψ`, and mine had a pushforward along a *different* morphism as its source. Record
both, or the next session reads "the mate is gone" as "almost done".

Related: [[measure-the-definition-not-the-api]] (unfold the thing before pricing its absence),
[[gate-inferred-from-an-absent-name]], [[wall-can-be-a-convention]].

**One Lean trap worth its own line.** Asserting a true-but-not-`rfl` iso equality does not *fail* —
`≪≫` is right-associated, so refactoring three of four factors differs by two `Category.assoc`, and
the kernel tries to `whnf` both composites and burns its heartbeat budget. **A `rfl` that times out is
evidence of neither hardness nor falsity**; it usually means associativity or a spelling difference
sitting in front of something expensive. Test with `Iso.ext` + `simp only [Category.assoc]` first.
